title: Disaster Related Extension of Deadlines Act
official_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to make the postponement of certain deadlines by reason of disasters applicable to the limitation on credit or refund, and to take postponements into account for purposes of sending collection notices.
likelihoodReason: Became Public Law 119-64 on December 26, 2025. Passed the House on March 31-April 1, 2025 and the Senate on December 11, 2025.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended

summary: When the IRS postpones tax deadlines because of a disaster, this makes that extra time also count toward the deadline for claiming a tax refund, and requires collection notices to reflect the postponement.
brief: Counts IRS disaster-related deadline postponements toward the refund-claim limitation period and in collection notices.

top_lines.headline: Disaster Deadline Postponements
subs: Disaster postponement periods count toward the refund-claim window
Collection notices must reflect disaster postponements
Applies to claims filed and notices issued after enactment

items.main: Names the Act the “Disaster Related Extension of Deadlines Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Postponement of Certain Deadlines by Reason of Disasters Made Applicable to Limitation on Credit or Refund

items.main: Treats IRS disaster-related deadline postponements as filing extensions for purposes of the time limit on tax credits or refunds.
items.detail: Adds subsection (f) to Section 7508A of the Internal Revenue Code so any period disregarded for filing a return is treated as an extension of time for filing under the refund-limitation rule (Section 6511(b)(2)(A)). It also amends Section 6303(b) so the last date for payment shown in a collection notice accounts for any period disregarded under Section 7508A. The changes apply to claims filed and notices issued after enactment.

gaps: The bill aligns disaster postponements with the refund-claim window but does not change the underlying disaster-postponement authority itself.
It applies to claims and notices going forward but does not address refunds already denied for filing outside the prior window.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Murphy
featured_quotes.text: I am blessed to live in eastern North Carolina, which is all too familiar with the devastation caused by natural disasters. For coastal Carolina, it is not a question of if but rather a question of when a hurricane will hit my district. We stick out far in the ocean and have a big bull's-eye target on us. We are still recovering from Hurricane Florence, which occurred in 2018. Despite being 7 years ago, there are still homes and businesses shuttered from the damage of that powerful hurricane.

modified: IRS disaster deadline postponements (Section 7508A) now count as filing extensions for the refund-claim limitation (Section 6511(b)(2)(A))
Collection notices (Section 6303(b)) must account for disaster-related postponement periods
